findings.title: Human-sample design cannot measure the quantity that justifies loosening a gate
findings.description:
The document's purpose is to move a judge "from advisory toward auto-gate". That decision depends mostly on the false-accept rate, meaning cases where the judge passed something a human would have failed. The sampling design leaves this unmeasured in three ways.
- **Unreviewed passes:** Gates run unattended, so the human only naturally sees escalations. Auto-passed artifacts are never seen unless the sampler deliberately draws them. "Which results are offered" is deferred as a "slice-level decision", yet it determines whether the headline number is valid. This is load-bearing, not detail.
- **Anchoring:** The doc doesn't say whether the operator sees the judge's verdict and score before giving their own call. If they do, agreement is inflated by anchoring. Blind capture is more costly and works against the "cheap, inline" goal.
- **One rater:** There is a single operator and no inter-rater reliability. The "ground truth" has unknown noise, and nothing in the doc acknowledges it.

Fix: make the sampling frame and blind-versus-informed capture architectural constraints, and require stratified sampling that includes auto-passed results.

findings.title: The evidence floor is undefined and may be unreachable at the stated sample sizes
findings.description:
The doc says samples will be "a handful per artifact level" and also requires a "minimum-evidence floor" before recommending any loosening. It never estimates what floor is statistically meaningful. For example, 20 of 20 agreements still leaves a 95% lower confidence bound near 83%. Every sample is further split by judge configuration (template version × model), so the effective n per key is smaller still.

As written, the feedback loop (the "Calibration feeds the gates" goal) may never fire. Alternatively, it fires on noise despite the "honest statistics" principle. The architecture should state a rough sample budget per key and the operator's expected review rate. Without them there is no way to tell whether the keystone is worth building.

findings.title: Two unrelated initiatives are bundled, and half depends on unbuilt work
findings.description:
The judge-calibration half (human samples, agreement and dispersion, threshold feedback) shares only the word "oracle" with the tech-debt-audit baseline and pre-emption prompt. The two have different inputs, different consumers (300 gates versus dispatch prompts), and different statistical shapes. A judge-vs-human agreement rate is a paired categorical comparison. Audit findings per project is a count of LLM-extracted items. The claim that "the reporting layer is built once" is unconvincing, since the only thing shared would be a generic storage layer.

The code-quality half also depends on 340's analysis pack. The frontmatter `dependencies: [100, 140, 300]` omits 340, and the doc lists 280 only as a candidate relationship. Recommendation: split the code-quality baseline and pre-emption prompt into their own initiative, or defer them. Doing so also removes the cross-project storage requirement from the keystone slice.

findings.title: The pre-emption delta measurement is circular and has no noise floor
findings.description:
- **Goodhart effect:** The pre-emption prompt targets "the issue classes the audit actually finds", and the same audit then measures success. Findings can fall because the prompt teaches to the test, not because code quality improved.
- **No noise floor:** The audit is LLM-authored and non-deterministic. The doc notes the variance but plans no repeat runs on identical code to establish a noise floor. With a "handful of projects" and observational before/after data, the delta may not be separable from run-to-run noise.
- **Contradictory goals:** The Design Goal says the baseline will prove "the metrology can detect an intervention's effect". The Technical Considerations say it is only "a credible directional signal, not causal proof". The architecture should settle which it is. It should also require either a held-out evaluator (a different audit prompt or model) or a same-code repeat-run variance measurement.

findings.title: "Read-side only" contradicts the write-side obligations the design needs
findings.description:
The principle "Read-side over 300's write path… does not modify the judging path… or the result models' write semantics" is not consistent with other parts of the doc.
- **Reserved `criteria` map:** The same bullet says 320 "populates" it, which is a write into 300's result model.
- **Judge-configuration identity:** Records must be keyed by "template identity/version, model". The doc never verifies that 300's provenance records a template version. If it doesn't, 320 must change the write path, which the Non-Goals prohibit.
- **Threshold feedback:** The "Calibration-to-threshold feedback" slice writes into 300's template and step-override threshold config. The doc doesn't establish that this config can be keyed by artifact level or judge configuration, or that it has a stable, machine-writable form. If thresholds are per-template only, per-level calibration cannot be applied.

The doc should name 300's actual extension points, and any gaps should be listed as explicit 300 changes.

findings.title: The storage and join decision is deferred although the keystone slice depends on it
findings.description:
The doc says storage "extends existing storage or adds a metrology store", possibly relating to 280, which has not started. It also requires cross-project aggregation, which 300's per-run persistence doesn't provide. Several unaddressed problems follow from this:
- **Join key:** The human sample must "attach unambiguously" to a specific judge result. Nothing says what the stable identity is, or what happens when a judge result is re-run, superseded, or pruned.
- **Project identity:** Cross-project data needs a stable project key that survives renames and moves.
- **Dispersion data:** Dispersion records join multiple results for one artifact. That is a different shape from a one-to-one sample-to-result record.

Without a stated direction (for example, a local SQLite file that is explicitly not 280), the keystone slice cannot be designed. A lightweight default should be chosen here, with 280 integration later.

findings.title: Dispersion is treated as a trust signal without addressing correlated judges
findings.description: "Judge-vs-judge dispersion" is meant to expose that "X overreaches, Y rubber-stamps". Dispersion shows only that judges differ. Without a human anchor it cannot say which one is wrong. Judges from the same model family will often agree with each other while being wrong, so low dispersion gives false comfort. The doc doesn't say how dispersion results combine with human agreement, or whether dispersion alone may influence threshold decisions. It also costs real tokens (multi-sample or `fan_out`) with no stated budget. Dispersion looks like a cuttable second phase: build human agreement first, and add dispersion only when it demonstrably changes a decision.

findings.title: Failure modes for capture, audit runs and stale data are not enumerated
findings.description:
The project's Failure-Mode Enumeration rule requires explicit, observable failure handling for each new I/O path. The doc has none for these cases:
- **Sample capture:** What happens if the operator's verdict references a result that no longer exists or was superseded? What if the same result is sampled twice with different verdicts?
- **Audit harness:** The cross-project run has no stated handling for timeouts, partial runs, a project that won't build, or cost overruns. Cost is also unbounded. Running an LLM audit across all squadron-managed projects, repeatedly, needs a budget cap.
- **Invalidation:** Calibration data goes stale on a template or model change, but no mechanism is described for retiring or segregating it. The doc only says "reports must not blend" incompatible configurations.
- **Over-fragmentation:** Keying by configuration means every template tweak resets n to zero, which compounds the evidence-floor problem above.

findings.title: Document hygiene
findings.description:
- The frontmatter `parent` path (`../project-guides/001-initiative-plan.squadron.md`) and the Related Work links are unverified in this review.
- "Interface parity if other surfaces are added" refers to a convention the doc doesn't define.
- The doc is explicit that the slices are exploratory. It should still say which slice gates the initiative's value: without a working threshold-feedback slice, the data layer and reporting have no consumer.

structured_findings.summary: Human-sample design cannot measure the quantity that justifies loosening a gate
The evidence floor is undefined and may be unreachable at the stated sample sizes
Two unrelated initiatives are bundled, and half depends on unbuilt work
The pre-emption delta measurement is circular and has no noise floor
"Read-side only" contradicts the write-side obligations the design needs
The storage and join decision is deferred although the keystone slice depends on it
Dispersion is treated as a trust signal without addressing correlated judges
Failure modes for capture, audit runs and stale data are not enumerated
